newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil gold output down six percent in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Brazil gold output down six percent in 1996.

text.p: Brazil gold production reached 60 tonnes in 1996, six percent down on the previous year, according to a review of the market completed by the Mines and Metallurgy Secretariat of the Mines and Energy Ministry.

Of this total, 41.14 tonnes were produced by companies, marking a slight increase on the 40.95 tonnes of industrial output in 1995. Production by wildcat miners, or garimpeiros, fell to 18.87 tonnes from 23.47 tonnes the previous year.
There are no official estimates yet of 1997 production, said Marcos Maron, general mineral co-ordinator at the secretariat.
The country's proven reserves rose dramatically to 1,700 tonnes at the end of 1996 from 800 tonnes registered in 1995.
A large part of this increase was due to a re-evaluation of the Salobo project in the northern state of Para, now estimated to have total reserves of 400 tonnes of gold, Maron said.

Gold will only be a by-product at the mine which is scheduled to start up in the year 2001 and should see annual production of 525,000 tonnes of electrolytic copper, eight tonnes of gold and 37 tonnes of silver.

Maron said the 1996 figure also does not include the estimated 150 tonnes which are expected to be found at the nearby Serra Leste gold mine, owned by Brazilian mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD).
The mine was announced last year but soundings by the company were hit for most of 1996 by protesting prospectors who claimed they were entitled to some of the mine's profits.
A report on the reserves is only now expected at the end of 1997 and so the mine has not yet been included, Maron said.
"These are seen for the time being as resources and not reserves," Maron said.
CVRD is Brazil's largest gold producer and output reached just over 18 tonnes in 1996 against 16.3 tonnes in 1995 according to the secretariat's review.
CVRD's partner in the Salobo project Mineracao Morro Velho saw a slight fall in output last year to 7.4 tonnes from 7.6 million in 1995.
Mineracao Morro Velho is controlled by the Brazilian arm of Minorco SA, which in turn is controlled by South Africa's Anglo-American and De Beers.
